issues: Postprandial and afternoon glucose excursions with time above range reaching up to 32.1% during afternoon hours
Hypoglycemia frequency of 5.1% below 70 mg/dL, concentrated in late evening and overnight periods
Total absence of logged carbohydrate entries, forcing the automated loop to rely entirely on UAM and SMB without proactive meal announcements
summary: Over a 14-day analysis period, time-in-range averaged 86.0% with a standard deviation of 39.7 mg/dL and a coefficient of variation of 32.6%. Overnight control shows strong stability with early morning glucose averaging around 90 to 105 mg/dL, though late-evening and early-morning hypoglycemia exceeds safety targets at 5.1% below 70 mg/dL. Afternoon hours experience significant hyperglycemia peaks due to unannounced meals and a reactive UAM-only delivery model.
education: Automated loops utilizing UAM and SMB rely heavily on timely glucose momentum detection when carbohydrates are unannounced, which can lead to delayed insulin delivery and postprandial spikes.

A flat insulin sensitivity factor across all hours combined with a conservative 10-hour duration of insulin action requires careful monitoring of active insulin on board to avoid stacking corrections.
strengths: High CGM data coverage of 98.7% with robust telemetry completeness across device statuses and loop executions
Strong overnight glucose stability and tight time-in-range during early morning fasting windows
Effective utilization of AAPS safety features including Dynamic ISF and UAM to modulate automated insulin delivery
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is excellent at 98.7% with minor gaps. Telemetry contains extensive device statuses and insulin treatments, but zero logged carb entries.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid entries out of 4,046 expected, 10 gaps with largest being 65 minutes, 2,315 treatments.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete absence of manual carb entry records.

analysis_steps.findings: Time in range is solid at 86.0%, but time below range of 5.1% exceeds the 4% safety threshold. Hypoglycemia clusters overnight and in evening hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%, glucose extremes reaching down to 41 mg/dL and up to 293 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of meal logging prevents direct attribution of lows to specific correction stacking or exercise.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates maintain stable glucose between 00:00 and 07:00 local time. Afternoon hours show rising averages up to 162.8 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly averages from 00:00 to 07:00 remain 90-106 mg/dL; afternoon hours 14:00-18:00 show elevated time above range.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unannounced meal impacts cannot be separated from basal adequacy without meal announcements.

analysis_steps.findings: Profile features a flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, a 10-hour DIA, and 5 CR segments. Automated Dynamic ISF compensates for the flat profile structure.
analysis_steps.evidence: Active ISF segment is constant at 56 mg/dL/U; dynamic sensitivity ratios fluctuate between 0.79 and 1.0.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Carb ratios cannot be audited directly due to unannounced meal practices.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are fully enabled with smb_always_enabled=true, supporting an unannounced meal strategy.
analysis_steps.evidence: AAPS configuration shows smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true, and 3-minute intervals.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled while Dynamic ISF is active at 70%. Safety limits are wide but appropriate.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true, max_basal=12 U/h, max_iob=25 U.

analysis_steps.findings: The user operates an unannounced meal strategy relying entirely on UAM and SMB rather than pre-meal boluses.
analysis_steps.evidence: Zero carb treatment entries in telemetry; postprandial rises handled reactively by automation.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carb entries to evaluate prebolus timing or bolus percentages.

analysis_steps.findings: Meal max absorption hours is set to 7 hours, matching slow absorption patterns associated with GLP-1 use.
analysis_steps.evidence: meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h, min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min; representative events show GLP-1 1.25mg administration.

analysis_steps.findings: Settings are stable and automation is compensating effectively for unannounced meals. Keeping current profile settings while introducing a pilot test of manual carb logging is the safest sequential path.
analysis_steps.evidence: Stable TIR of 86.0%, active Dynamic ISF and UAM, absence of logged carbs.

recommendations.title: Pilot Manual Carb Logging
recommendations.description: To address afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia peaks caused by reactive UAM responses, test logging carbohydrate entries and manual meal boluses for a 3-day period to evaluate whether proactive delivery reduces time above range.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Overall time in range is strong at 86.0% and overnight glucose is stable. Automation via Dynamic ISF and UAM is compensating for flat profile settings, and changing dependent parameters without baseline carb logging data is unsupported.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor afternoon postprandial glucose excursions during a 3-day period of manual carb logging before considering profile adjustments.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings unchanged and verify loop performance with proactive meal entry.

Evening basal segment maintains acceptable control. No conflicting evidence requires alteration.
Absence of logged carb entries prevents audit of carb ratios. Current value must be kept.
Carb ratio cannot be evaluated without manual meal data. Keeping current value avoids premature changes.
No meal records exist to test daytime carb ratios. Current setting is retained.
Afternoon spikes relate to unannounced meal absorption rather than validated CR error. Keep current value.
Evening carb ratio lacks direct verification data. Keep current value.

Overnight target of 90 mg/dL supports stable fasting control. Keep current setting.
Daytime target of 100 mg/dL provides a safe buffer during active hours. Keep current setting.
Night target transition maintains stable late-evening glucose. Keep current setting.
10-hour DIA provides conservative insulin stacking protection alongside GLP-1 use. Keep current setting.
Both SMB and UAM are appropriately enabled to support unannounced meal handling.
Activation conditions match the unannounced meal strategy. Keep current configuration.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain the current automated UAM and SMB delivery model while piloting manual carbohydrate logging for high-carbohydrate meals to reduce afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia peaks.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user successfully operates an unannounced meal strategy with strong overnight control, but reactive UAM delivery leads to unavoidable postprandial delays during afternoon meals.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe postprandial glucose peaks during a 3-day test of manual meal announcements.

exceptions.pattern: GLP-1 injection days with delayed gastric emptying
exceptions.suggestion: Retain extended absorption settings (7 hours) to prevent late insulin stacking.
exceptions.rationale: GLP-1 therapy slows digestion, shifting carbohydrate absorption windows later.

implementation_steps: Review current data findings and safety overview with the care team.
Keep all baseline profile segments and AAPS automation settings unchanged.
Initiate a 3-day pilot of manual carbohydrate logging for meals to evaluate impact on afternoon postprandial excursions.
Monitor glucose closely for any signs of increased hypoglycemia risk when testing meal announcements.
